title: AI Presentation Makers for Consultants — Jon Martin
description: Gamma, Beautiful.ai, and Pitch compared for consultants: prices, free plans and trials, AI credit limits, and export options.
dek: Three tools that turn an outline into a client-ready deck, for consultants who'd rather spend the time on the thinking than on aligning boxes.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This is for an independent consultant or a two-to-five-person advisory shop that builds proposals, workshop decks, and readouts every week, often on a deadline.

The AI part is useful for a first draft. What matters more is how much AI you get before hitting a limit, whether the output looks like your brand, and whether you can hand the client a file they can open.

Start with Gamma if you want the fastest path from a prompt to a full draft. Pick Beautiful.ai if layout is where you lose time and you want unlimited AI on one plan. Pick Pitch if you want a free plan with unlimited decks and room for a small team later.
Draft the same deck in each tool's free plan or trial: your last proposal, rebuilt from its outline. That will tell you more than any feature list.
Gamma starts {{fact:gamma.free}}. Plus is {{fact:gamma.plus}}. Pro is {{fact:gamma.pro}}. Per Gamma, {{fact:gamma.annual}}, and {{fact:gamma.per_user}}.
Gamma supports {{fact:gamma.export}}, so clients don't need a Gamma account to open your work. Note that {{fact:gamma.free_credits}}, so the free plan is for testing, not for steady use.
Beautiful.ai Pro is {{fact:beautifulai.pro}}. Team is {{fact:beautifulai.team}}. There's {{fact:beautifulai.trial}}.
Its strength is {{fact:beautifulai.layouts}}, along with {{fact:beautifulai.ai}}. It also supports {{fact:beautifulai.ppt}}, which helps if you're moving old decks over.
Pitch is {{fact:pitch.free}}. Plus is {{fact:pitch.plus}}. Team is {{fact:pitch.team}}. Per Pitch, {{fact:pitch.annual}}.
If you run out of AI on a paid plan, Pitch sells {{fact:pitch.credits}}. As for trials, Pitch offers {{fact:pitch.trial}}.

Look at the AI allowance, not just the price. Credit-based plans charge per generation, and a heavy week of proposals can use a month's allowance. Unlimited plans cost more up front but don't surprise you.
Then check the handoff. Many clients want an editable file. If yours do, test the export on a real deck and open it in the client's tool before you commit.
Last, think about brand. Custom fonts, colors, and themes keep every deck looking like your firm, and they sit on different plans in each tool.
Feed the tool your outline, not a one-line prompt. The structure of your argument is the part a client is paying for, and the AI should only fill in the layout.
Check every chart and number the tool adds. A generated slide can look finished and still be wrong.

faq.q: Which AI presentation maker has a free plan?
faq.a: Gamma and Pitch do. Gamma starts {{fact:gamma.free}}. Pitch is {{fact:pitch.free}}. Beautiful.ai offers {{fact:beautifulai.trial}} instead of a free plan for most users.
Gamma supports {{fact:gamma.export}}. Pitch includes PowerPoint export on Plus.
On Gamma's free plan, {{fact:gamma.free_credits}}. Pitch sells {{fact:pitch.credits}}. Beautiful.ai lists {{fact:beautifulai.ai}}.

closing: Rebuild one real proposal in each tool, open the export the way your client would, and pick the one that saved you the most time.
